maya: Kicking off perf validation for the AP-SOUTHEAST-1 GPU cluster bring-up. Focus: kernel/driver checks, NCCL/PCIe health, and throughput/latency baselining. Will paste quick outputs and baseline numbers here.

diego: Quick checklist to run on every provisioned node: 
- sudo nvidia-smi -q
- uname -r; apt list --installed | grep nvidia
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
- lspci -vvv | grep -i nvidia

infra-bot: deploybot: node-provisioning complete for ap-southeast-1-gpupool-1 (12 nodes). ansible run: 2024-06-15T03:12Z.

samira: Ran nvidia-smi summary on node gpu-08:```
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-abc123)
Driver Version: 525.105.17
CUDA Version: 12.1
PCIe Gen: 4
FB Memory Usage: 3.2GiB / 40GiB
Power Draw: 280W
```

kai: saw this in dmesg on gpu-03 earlier:```
[  12.345678] NVRM: GPU at 0000:5e:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  12.345679] nvidia 0000:5e:00.0: GPU multi-function device detected, disabling ECC reporting
```
This might indicate a flaky PCIe link or BIOS PCIe ASPM settings.

diego: For the "fallen off the bus" errors, steps we used last time:
1) Re-seat PCIe riser (if on-prem) or reprovision host NIC firmware in cloud image.
2) Ensure kernel boot args: "pci=nomsi" avoided; prefer enabling "pcie_aspm=force" only after testing.
3) Reinstall driver with dkms: `sudo apt-get install --reinstall nvidia-driver-525` then reboot.

maya: Running microbenchmarks across 8 GPUs (local inference harness):
Command: `./bench/llm_throughput --model=gpt2-small --batch=8 --seq=512 --gpus=8 --warmup=100 --iter=500`
Results (avg over 5 runs):
- tokens/sec: 78,400
- p50 latency (per batch): 42ms
- p95 latency (per batch): 87ms
- avg GPU util: 92%
Notes: throughput matches our expected baseline within 4% of eu-west numbers at same instance sku.

samira: Ran NCCL bandwidth test between the 8 GPUs across two hosts: `nccl-tests/build/all_reduce_perf -b 4M -e 128M -f 2 -g 4`
Observed ~24 GB/s aggregate, ~12% lower than lab baseline. dmesg shows a few TCP retransmits on bond0. Suspect MTU mismatch on the 100GbE link.
Suggested sysctls (applied on both hosts):
```
sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=268435456
sudo sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=268435456
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_rmem="4096 87380 268435456"
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem="4096 65536 268435456"
```
Also verify `ip link show` MTU=9000 on all switches and hosts.

ops-oncall: I'll take handoff for the canary rollout tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Need a short runbook + rollback plan. Can we capture the exact validation gates? @maya @diego

maya: Canary validation gates (to include in runbook):
- Node health: all nodes report Driver Version 525.105.17 and CUDA 12.1 via nvidia-smi (quick script ok).
- PCIe/Dmesg: no "GPU has fallen off the bus" messages in last 10m.
- NCCL: all_reduce_perf >= 26 GB/s per-host aggregate (or within -10% of baseline).
- Microbench throughput: tokens/sec within -10% of eu-west baseline for same sku.
- Latency: p95 < 120ms at intended batch sizes.
- Network: no retransmits and MTU=9000 end-to-end.
- Cost check: initial pool = 12 nodes; recommend 20% buffer for autoscale. Estimated monthly cost delta: ~$9,400 for 12 nodes (gpu-sku) — flag finance if +10%.

diego: Rollback plan:
1) Disable new pool in routing (re-route traffic to eu-west/pinned capacity).
2) Drain nodes in new cluster from load balancer.
3) Revert any sysctl tuning if it caused instability: restore from /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood-default.conf.
4) If driver rollback needed: apt-get install nvidia-driver-515 and reboot (documented in ops playbook).

maya: Action items:
- diego: finalize small script that checks nvidia-smi, dmesg grep, nccl perf and posts summary to #eng-infra (due EOD).
- samira: validate MTU across switches and patch switch configs if needed, then rerun all_reduce (due in 2h).
- kai: inspect gpu-03 hardware log and coordinate with cloud vendor support for PCIe "fallen off" trace (start now).
- ops-oncall: prepare canary runbook with the gates above, include exact commands and rollback (due by 08:00 UTC tomorrow).

maya: If anyone hits flaky PCIe or driver mismatch during canary, @ops-oncall please pause promotion and ping #eng-sre. :eyes: 

diego: Also note – add automated nightly perf collection to compare baselines across regions (will open a ticket). :memo:
